title: Decentralized tail-tracing and heatmap views for route/model/region
creator: Liang Chen
description:
Problem: Our current latency dashboards provide aggregate quantiles but lack a lightweight, decentralized way to inspect tail events in context. Engineers need to quickly pivot from a p99 spike to example request traces, token/sec patterns, and sequence-length-conditioned heatmaps per route/model/region without overloading telemetry storage.

Goal: Add a distributed tail-tracing pipeline and per-route/model/region heatmap panels that surface representative tail requests, token/sec rhythm, and p95/p99 surfaces. The system should: (1) sample and store compact tail traces and key metrics at the edge, (2) emit heatmap rollups (sequence length vs. tokens/sec vs. latency) to the telemetry stream, and (3) power alerting/regression detectors that combine rolling-basis p95/p99 drift scoring with example trace links for root-cause triage.

Why this matters: On-call and SRE operate by bouncing between dashboards and PRs; having contextual, lightweight trace artifacts tied to heatmap clusters significantly reduces mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-fix for model-serving regressions introduced by kernel changes, batching policy changes, or quantization flips.

Scope:
- Instrumentation: add edge-side compact tail trace emitter, with configurable sampling rate and sequence-length bucketing.
- Aggregation: heatmap rollups emitted as pre-aggregated tiles (sequenceLenBucket, tokensPerSecBucket, latencyQuantileBucket) to the quantile telemetry topic.
- Storage: short-lived example trace store (14 days) with index by route/model/region and trace fingerprint.
- UI: Console panels: 1) heatmap explorer with brush-selection to list example traces, 2) tail-trace viewer (compact token-level timeline + KV cache hit markers + batching window boundaries), 3) regression timeline combining p95/p99 drift score and sample traces.
- Regression detection: implement drift detector using EWMA of p95/p99 per-slice + outlier scoring; when a slice's drift score crosses threshold, file a regression watcher and attach top-3 tail traces.
acceptance_criteria: Edge emitter can be configured per-region and per-route with sampling_rate and sequence_len_buckets
Heatmap rollups appear in telemetry topic with keys: route, model_version, region, seq_bucket, tps_bucket, latency_quantile
Console shows interactive heatmap; brushing results in list of 10 representative tail traces with links to the trace viewer
Trace viewer displays token-level timeline, batching windows, and KV cache hit/miss markers for sampled traces
Automated drift detector raises regression watcher PR when p95/p99 drift score & sample size thresholds are met
End-to-end benchmark: synthetic harness can reproduce a seeded p99 regression and the system surfaces it with <15 minutes latency
implementation_notes: Edge emitter: lightweight protobuf payload (~1.2KB avg) with compressed token offsets and event timestamps. Use existing edge sidecar pipeline; add config flag emit_tail_traces=true
Sampling strategy: stratified by route*model*sequence_len_bucket to avoid small-slice starvation; default sampling_rate=0.002 for high-volume routes, 0.02 for low-volume routes
Heatmap bucketing: sequence_len: 0-128/129-512/513-2048/2049+, tokens/sec buckets exponential (0-20,20-50,50-200,200+), latency quantiles stored as p50/p90/p95/p99 per tile
Rollup emission: tile size 5m -> aggregator emits to quantile-tiles topic. Use existing telemetry producer lib and ensure backpressure safeguards (circuit breaker per-producer)
Trace store: 14 day TTL in DynamoDB + compressed payloads in S3; index entries in Dynamo by route|model|region|trace_fingerprint
Console: new Heatmap panel module will reuse existing frontend heatmap component; add server-side endpoints to fetch tiles and trace lists. Keep materialization server-side to reduce browser load
Regression detector: implement as a streaming job reading quantile-tiles -> compute EWMA drift per slice with configurable alpha; persist scores to alerts index and attach top-k traces by severity
Synthetic harness integration: extend inferbench to annotate runs with a deterministic perturbation token delay so we can validate detector sensitivity and false-positive rates
Telemetry cost considerations: shrink trace payloads and limit default sampling to control storage cost; provide admin toggles for raising sample rates for debug windows
